items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: The first time I took Judge to a tavern, I was just running off my mouth, talking to people, drunkards and so on.

ctx.x: infested with bars, 212. It's the record. And you could check with the Police; it was publicized in the paper. Door after door after door down the block, there's bars, bars, bars, bars. Swedish bars, where the Swedish sailors come in, and the Iranian sailors, the Mexican sailors. Every ship that plies the world, they could go in a joint in Hoboken and find a be-at-home welcome. And that's what Hoboken is all about.

And when I began to hustle, I wanted to learn... I fond out that if you never get to the mike and never hit the footlights, you rarely would make money. You'd always be the sideman. So I decided somewhere I was going to learn to talk and say something. The first time I took Judge to a tavern, I was just running off my mouth, talking to people, drunkards and so on. He'd say, "Why do you talk so much?" That's something you have to learn, to talk to the public. And that was my way of learning. Now I'll go anywhere…
